source.title: AsFT: Anchoring Safety During LLM Fine-Tuning Within Narrow Safety Basin
source.authors: Shuo Yang; Qihui Zhang; Yu-Yang Liu; Yue Huang; Xiao-Jun Jia; Kunpeng Ning; Jiayu Yao; Jigang Wang; Hailiang Dai; Yibing Song; Li Yuan

record.file_problem: Whole paper text is present. The text contains some apparent extraction inconsistencies in table references and an abstract result that differs from later reported comparisons, but these do not prevent reading the relevant results.
record.tranche_reason: The study fine-tunes aligned models with harmful data and measures unsafe-output rates, testing the harmful-fine-tuning effect. It uses its own datasets, settings, and safety-preservation method rather than explicitly replicating the original study’s full recipe.
record.gate_note: The paper reports harmful-score outcomes after harmful fine-tuning, including poison-ratio, sample-number, dataset, and model comparisons. The clean condition in Table 2 is a fine-tuned clean-data reference, not an untrained-model result. Benign-only fine-tuning results lack an untrained reference for determining whether benign tuning raised harmful compliance. The paper’s jailbreak evaluation is described only as robust performance, without quantitative results, and does not test compliant-opening prefills or decoding changes. Cited results from other work are not recorded.
record.test_reason: A defense paper. Its vanilla-SFT baseline gives harmful-score results for safety-tuned chat models fine-tuned on task data mixed with 50–200 harmful examples, against a clean-SFT reference (Table 2). That bears on V1 in a poisoned-task-data setting. No other version is measured.
record.authors_conclusion: Largely correct. The authors also claim that harmful update directions are nearly orthogonal to the aligned-minus-base direction (a 'narrow safety basin'). They report that AsFT, which penalizes orthogonal updates, gives lower harmful scores and comparable or higher accuracy than SFT, Lisa, SafeInstr, BEA and Safe LoRA across 8 datasets and 4 models.
record.recipe_differences: Uses harmful-data fine-tuning and unsafe-output evaluation, with mixtures of harmful and benign task data; the study centers on directional parameter constraints and does not state that it is a replication of the original recipe. It does not measure response-token KL or test opening-prefill bypasses.
record.method_sensitivity: Reported unsafe-output scores vary with poison ratio (Table 2), harmful-data sample number (Table 3), harmful dataset (Table 4), and model architecture (Table 6).

fits_no_version.finding: The harmful fine-tuning update direction is nearly orthogonal to the aligned-minus-base weight direction (cosine ~6e-4 vs ~8.5e-3 for random). Effective perturbation length is much larger along the alignment direction than along the harmful direction, across Llama-2, Qwen-2 and Gemma-2.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Safety in parameter space is anisotropic: updates orthogonal to the alignment direction degrade safety far faster than updates along it.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the tabulated harmful scores or direction measurements. The clean SFT reference is not an untrained aligned model, and the paper does not provide an untreated comparison for its benign-only fine-tuning outcomes. Several architecture and harmful-dataset results therefore show post-fine-tuning scores without a direct pre-fine-tuning reference. The jailbreak robustness statement is not accompanied by quantitative results in the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded Table 2–6 results for AsFT and other defense methods, fine-tuning accuracy values, and Table 5 benign-only SFT outcomes. They either report comparisons among defense methods or, for benign-only SFT, lack an untrained reference needed to establish an increase in harmful compliance. Also excluded the non-quantitative jailbreak statement and figure-only hyperparameter/ablation curves; the paper’s explicit qualitative conclusions about the directional landscape are summarized under fits_no_version.

untested.parts: Pure harmful-only fine-tuning, without task-data mixing. Refusal rate itself, rather than an audited unsafe-output proportion. Pre-fine-tuning harmfulness for any model.
No benign-only result compared against the untuned aligned model.
No per-token KL or position analysis.
Jailbreaks (LLM-DRA, ArtPrompt) are mentioned only qualitatively, for AsFT. No prefill or decoding tests.
Studies a global alignment direction, not a small set of weights or ranks.
AsFT is a direction regularizer, not token-depth deepening.

missing.what: Vanilla SFT harmful scores for Llama-2-7B-Chat at p=0.1 on other fine-tuning tasks: SST2 48.00, GSM8K 56.00, AlpacaEval 20.40. These are poisoned mixtures, not benign-only as rows_left_out states. No clean reference is given for these tasks.
Harmful-data proportion raised to 60%, reported only qualitatively for AsFT. The SFT numbers are not given.

record.verdict_notes: The reader mislabels Table 5 as benign-only SFT; it is poisoned (p=0.1) fine-tuning on different tasks. The abstract's 'up to 7.60%' reduction conflicts with the 17.44% stated in the introduction. Other models (Llama-3 73.60, Qwen-2 49.20, Gemma-2 32.00) show high post-fine-tuning HS but lack clean references, so no verdict is given for them. The Table 3 sample-number rows at n≠1000 have no matched clean reference.

versions.untested_parts: Tests harmful-data fine-tuning with 50–200 harmful examples in Table 2’s n=1000 setting and reports further harmful-data settings. It does not show refusal removal almost entirely in that setting; the reported measure is an audited unsafe-output proportion, not a direct refusal rate.
The paper reports harmful scores after clean/benign fine-tuning, but does not compare those outcomes with an untrained aligned model or otherwise establish that benign fine-tuning raised compliance.
No per-token KL divergence or response-position distribution comparison.

No compliant-opening prefill or decoding-change test. The paper mentions LLM-DRA and ArtPrompt evaluations but gives no quantitative results and does not report that those attacks work by getting past response-opening tokens.
The paper examines global alignment and perturbation directions, not whether a small set of weights or ranks carries safety.
Does not test why safety would be shallow or relate shallowness to data or training objective.
AsFT constrains parameter-update directions, but the paper does not test spreading safety beyond early response tokens or whether token-depth training holds up.

relationships.condition: Llama-2-7B-Chat, AGNEWS, n=1000, 50–200 harmful examples mixed into task data, LoRA SFT
relationships.reason: HS rises from 2.40 (clean) to 16.40–46.80, rising with poison ratio (largest at 200 examples). This is far from full loss of refusal (R1–R5, R7, R11, R15).
relationships.display_finding: The harmful score rose from 2.40 with clean data to 16.40–46.80, growing with the number of harmful examples and peaking at 200, far from full loss of refusal.
